1.title: AI Workloads and Scenarios
1.text: Welcome to Module four: A I Workloads and Scenarios. It covers the exam area Identify A I concepts and capabilities. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. The six workloads. Generative A I. Agentic A I. Text analysis. Speech. Computer vision. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Identify A I concepts and capabilities (forty to forty-five percent). Exam format: a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes; check the exam page for the time. Validated against: the official A I nine oh one study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: The six workloads
1.text: The six workloads. An A I workload is a kind of problem that A I solves. The exam gives a business scenario and asks which workload it is. Learn each one with its input, output and a typical example.

1.title: The six workloads, continued
1.text: The six workloads. Generative A I. Input: A prompt (text, sometimes images or audio). Output: New text, code, images or audio. Example scenario: Write a product description; answer questions in a chat. Agentic A I. Input: A goal and instructions. Output: Actions taken with tools, then a result. Example scenario: An assistant that looks up an order, checks stock and replies. Text analysis. Input: Text. Output: Facts about the text: key phrases, entities, sentiment, summary. Example scenario: Find what customers complain about in reviews.

1.title: The six workloads, continued
1.text: The six workloads. Speech. Input: Spoken audio, or text. Output: Text from audio, or audio from text. Example scenario: Transcribe a meeting; read a message aloud. Computer vision. Input: Images or video. Output: Captions, tags, objects, text in images. Example scenario: Describe a photo; read a street sign. Information extraction. Input: Documents, images, audio, video. Output: Structured fields (Jason) or searchable text. Example scenario: Pull invoice number, date and total from invoices.

1.title: The six workloads, continued
1.text: The six workloads. The figure shows this: The six A I workloads: input, output and example.

1.title: Generative AI
1.text: Generative A I. Generative A I creates content from a prompt. Text: draft email, summarize, translate, answer, write code. Images: create a picture from a description. The result is new, not looked up. It can be wrong (Module two), so grounding and review matter.

1.title: Agentic AI
1.text: Agentic A I. An A I agent is a software application built on generative A I with three parts. A large language model. The "brain" that reasons about the request. Instructions. A system prompt that defines the agent's role and behavior. Tools. What the agent can use: knowledge tools (search, files) and action tools (call an A P I, run code).

1.title: Agentic AI, continued
1.text: Agentic A I. Agentic A I means the agent decides which tools to use and takes steps toward a goal, instead of only answering. Multi-agent systems have several agents that collaborate, each with its own specialty. Exam tip: Generative equals produces content. Agentic equals plans and acts with tools (look up, calculate, call a service). If the scenario says "checks the order status and updates the ticket", think agent.

1.title: Text analysis
1.text: Text analysis. Text analysis (natural language processing) extracts meaning from existing text. Keyword (key phrase) extraction. What are the main topics? Entity detection. Which people, places, organizations, dates and amounts are named? Sentiment analysis. Is the opinion positive, negative, neutral or mixed? Summarization. What is the short version? Language detection. Which language is this? Exam tip: Check the input and the output to pick the workload: text in, facts about it out is text analysis; text in, new text out is generative A I.

1.title: Speech
1.text: Speech. Audio to text. Name: Speech recognition (speech to text). Example: Captions and meeting notes. Text to audio. Name: Speech synthesis (text to speech). Example: A voice assistant reads the answer. Spoken language to another language. Name: Speech translation. Example: Live interpretation.

1.title: Computer vision
1.text: Computer vision. Computer vision understands images and video: describe a picture (caption), tag its contents, detect objects and their positions, read text in images (O C R), detect people. Image-generation models work the other way: they create an image from text.

1.title: Information extraction
1.text: Information extraction. Information extraction turns unstructured content (documents, forms, images, audio, video) into structured data or text that can be searched. Example: receipts and invoices become fields such as vendor, date and total; call recordings become a transcript and a summary.

1.title: Choose the workload
1.text: Choose the workload. "write", "draft", "chat", "create a picture". Generative A I (image creation equals generative or image generation). "decide which step to take and call the system". Agentic A I. "what do customers feel about, ", "find names and dates in text". Text analysis. "transcribe", "read aloud", "voice commands". Speech. "describe the photo", "find the cars", "read the sign". Computer vision. "pull the total from invoices", "get fields from forms". Information extraction. Exam tip: Check the input and output. Text in, facts about it out equals text analysis. Text in, new text out equals generative A I. Document in, fields out equals information extraction.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants to learn whether thousands of product reviews are positive or negative. Which workload is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Text analysis. Sentiment analysis is a text analysis technique.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. The team wants an assistant that checks stock, looks up an order and then emails the customer by calling company systems. Which workload fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Agentic A I. An agent uses tools to take actions toward a goal.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A finance team wants invoice numbers, dates and totals pulled from scanned invoices into a database. Which workload is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Information extraction. Turning documents into structured fields is information extraction.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A tablet app must read a news article aloud to a visually impaired user. Which capability is needed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Speech synthesis. Speech synthesis converts text to spoken audio.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A mobile app must identify the objects in a photo and say where each one is. Which workload is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Computer vision. Object detection is a computer vision task.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A marketing team asks a model to write three slogan ideas for a new tent. Which workload is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Generative A I. Creating new text from a prompt is generative A I.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the six workloads in this module. Answer: Generative A I, agentic A I, text analysis, speech, computer vision, information extraction. Question two. What three parts make an A I agent? Answer: A large language model, instructions and tools. Question three. What are the two kinds of agent tools? Answer: Knowledge tools and action tools.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Speech recognition turns what into what? Answer: Spoken audio into text. Question five. Which workload outputs structured fields from documents? Answer: Information extraction. Question six. What does a multi-agent system have? Answer: Several agents that collaborate, each with its own specialty.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Generative A I: creates new content from a prompt. Agentic A I: agent equals model plus instructions plus tools; takes actions toward a goal. Text analysis: keywords, entities, sentiment, summary, language. Speech: recognition (audio to text), synthesis (text to audio), translation. Computer vision: caption, tags, objects, O C R, people; image generation creates images. Information extraction: documents, images, audio, video to structured fields or searchable text. In the next module, we continue the course.
